newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ARA storage firms say area is flush with fuel oil.
newsitem.headline: ARA storage firms say area is flush with fuel oil.

text.p: Independent storage companies in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp area say stocks of high sulphur fuel oil in the area have risen noticeably in the last two weeks.
"(Fuel oil stocks) seem to be about a couple of 100,000 tonnes more than normal," said one storer.
"I wouldn't want to put a number on them, but they're higher than expected," said another.
One more added he was fully booked next week.

The current status of stocks is linked to the low price of fuel oil barges and bunkers which have fallen $22/$23 a tonne, or almost 20 percent, since January 7. Even a mild return of bullishness on Thursday only added around $3 to the price.
Quite whether prices are low because stocks are high or stocks high due to low prices is, according to independent storers, a chicken-and-egg conundrum.
"People do seem rather unwilling to sell at the moment," one storer said.
What seems beyond doubt is that since the end of autumn, refinery output in northwest Europe has been approaching full capacity as the price of gas oil in particular has soared.

"In the last couple of months, inventories have been reasonably high, but throughput has also been high. In the last couple of weeks, however, the market has collapsed," a storer said. "Now we're faced with quite some inventories without nominations."
